https://www.budapesttimes.hu/hungary/to-.text: The Budapest Times To serve and protect — minister vows to clean up the ranks The Hungarian state must regain people's trust in the lawful functioning of the state, and the Ministry of Interior must bear the lion's share of that responsibility — the interior minister declared on Tuesday in Budapest, when he announced promotions and presented decorations to police, disaster management and prison service personnel on the occasion of the national holiday. Gábor Pósfai said that those working in law enforcement organisations provide security for all of us, and that it is the duty of the Hungarian state to provide them with stability and, equally, security in return. He stressed that the Hungarian state exists for Hungarian citizens, so that everyone can feel at home. Since the formation of the new government, intensive work in this spirit has been under way at the Ministry of Interior as well, and progress has already been achieved in a number of areas. New leaders have been entrusted with mandates and appointments, and new ideas and expectations have also been set out, he indicated. The interior minister described changing the existing organisational culture as essential. He said the new approach — one of treating each other as partners — applies to everyone and “starts with the minister.” Accountability, responsibility and honesty must be present at every level of the organisations, he declared. “I promise and expect straightforwardness, honesty and integrity, and as minister I can state that this is what you can count on from me and my fellow leaders as well,” he said. Gábor Pósfai pledged that they would do everything in their power to improve working conditions, technical requirements, and professional recognition. Their goal is for employees to be able to carry out their work with more modern equipment in the future, and for their social recognition to be reflected in their salaries and benefits, he said. He stressed that in recent times a number of reforms had been launched that could make their effects felt in the short term: reducing administration, eliminating redundancies, and modernising the command structure all serve the goal of allowing those on active duty to focus on their actual tasks. Pay reform, career pathways, inequalities between personnel categories, unnecessary administration, and the deteriorating condition of equipment and uniforms are all areas in which they are currently working on solutions, he listed. The minister asked for the patience of the personnel in addressing the shortcomings of many years, indicating that in the coming weeks he would bring his proposal for a comprehensive pay reform before the government, that the issue of the inherited staff shortage would be treated as a priority, and that the name of the fire service would be restored. He put it this way: 20 August is not only the celebration of the founding of the state, but also a reminder — a reminder of responsibility towards the community. The legacy of King Saint István is not merely the creation of the Hungarian state, but the recognition that a country is only strong if those who serve it are not indifferent. “This is especially true in law enforcement, because if we do not pay attention, if we do not act, then those who have no one left but us will be left without help,” added Gábor Pósfai, who expressed his thanks for the service of law enforcement personnel. At the ceremony, 109 law enforcement personnel were able to receive their promotion documents, as well as decorations and material awards. Gábor Pósfai promoted Tamás Mecser, the national chief of police, to the rank of police major general. Szabolcs Tóth, director general of the National Security Service, was promoted to national security major general, and Norbert Tamás Baricska, Budapest’s chief of police, was promoted to police brigadier general.
